SQLite scans every row and checks the requested column for a full table scan.
SQLite adds an index on the searched column to use indexed lookup.

assertions.subject: representation.ordered_index_x
assertions.value: entries are ordered by indexed columns

provenance.evidence: The logical index view stores indexed content in order.

assertions.subject: operation.index_lookup_x
assertions.value: searches the ordered index

provenance.evidence: The documentation describes binary search on the index.

assertions.subject: operation.index_lookup_x
assertions.value: consults the original table after the index search in the ordinary non-covering case

provenance.evidence: The documentation describes a row lookup in the original table after finding the index entry.

assumptions: the index is not covering

assertions.subject: representation.ordered_index_x
assertions.value: contains all columns needed for a particular query and avoids consulting the original table for covered columns

provenance.evidence: A covering index contains all columns needed for a query and avoids the original table lookup.

assumptions: the query's required columns are all covered

assertions.subject: representation.ordered_index_x
assertions.value: can satisfy ORDER BY by scanning the index

provenance.evidence: SQLite scans an ORDER BY index in the requested direction.

assumptions: the index order matches the ORDER BY terms

assertions.subject: operation.build_ordered_index
assertions.value: automatic index construction is O(N log N)

provenance.evidence: SQLite compares O(N log N) construction with O(N) scans.

assumptions: automatic indexes are enabled
N is the table entry count

assertions.subject: operation.build_ordered_index
assertions.value: builds a query-time index when estimated lookup count exceeds log(N)

provenance.evidence: SQLite expects the indexed lookup to be used more than log N times before building a query-time index.

assumptions: automatic indexes are enabled

assertions.subject: operation.build_ordered_index
assertions.value: estimated number of indexed lookup uses

provenance.evidence: The planner's decision depends on its estimate that the indexed lookup will be used more than log N times.

assumptions: N is the table entry count
the planner has an estimate of repeated lookup use
